events.title: Canada jobs (Sep)

USD/CAD rose to ~1.4275, near 52-week highs.

events.title: Canada foreign securities purchases (Aug)
events.why: Foreign demand for Canadian securities — capital-flow texture for the loonie.
events.if_beat: Strong: foreign bid intact — mild CAD support.
events.if_miss: Weak: foreign bid fading.
events.actual: -C$17.31B (vs +C$23.59B fcst); first monthly net divestment of 2026
events.outcome: Big miss vs +C$23.59B forecast: foreigners sold a net C$17.31B of Canadian securities in August — the first monthly divestment of 2026 — led by a record C$17.5B cut in federal government debt securities (C$11.2B bonds, C$6.3B paper), partially offset by +C$7.6B corporate bonds and +C$1.6B provincials. Foreigners also sold C$9.9B of Canadian equities. Canadian investors bought C$23.9B in foreign securities (C$28.9B of US shares) — net C$41.21B outflow from the Canadian economy. YTD foreign investment still strong at +C$161.6B vs +C$27.1B in 2025. Capital-flow texture for the Oct 28 BoC, not a policy game-changer.

sources.label: Dow Jones via Morningstar (Oct 16): Foreigners Sold C$17.3 Billion of Canadian Securities in August, Targeting Federal Government Debt
